production.note: US model year 1987 only. Quote (Street Muscle, Jim Campisano): "Buick made 547 GNXs in 1987." Classic Industries: "A total of 547 GNXs were produced", 1987 only (classicindustries-gnx).

body.note: Conceptcarz page title: "1987 Buick Regal Coupe". Sports Car Market describes the Grand National as a "mid-size rear-drive sedan" (in the sense of a mid-size car); Conceptcarz is cited for the body.

displacementL.note: "3.8 Liter V6 engine" (Classic Industries). Sports Car Market's "a turbocharged 231-ci V6" describes the earlier Grand National engine, not specifically the GNX. No opened page printed the cc figure.

aspiration.note: "a special Garrett T-3 turbocharger"; single turbo.

transmission.note: "Turbo Hydramatic 200-4R transmission was modified with a custom torque converter and fluid cooler." The four-speed count is read from the 200-4R designation; no opened page states it. Classic Industries: "Beefed up TH200-4R transmission".

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (articles, no Buick document opened). Buick's 1987 US rating (SAE net). Quote (Sports Car Market, Tom Glatch): "Buick rated this engine at 276 hp at 4,400 rpm, but in truth it probably produced over 300 hp." Street Muscle (Jim Campisano): "Horsepower was rated at 276 and torque 360 lbs-ft." (streetmuscle-gnx). Classic Industries (Patrick McCarthy): "276 horsepower" (classicindustries-gnx). Conceptcarz (Daniel Vaughan): "conservatively rated at 276 horsepower and 360 lb-ft of torque" (conceptcarz-gnx).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (single article, tested-style figure). Quote (Street Muscle, Jim Campisano): "If you use Car and Driver's times and 3,545-lb curbweight (minus driver), that's somewhere around 285-294 horsepower". A curb weight used by Street Muscle alongside Car and Driver's times; the article does not explicitly attribute the weight. Not a Buick figure. Only one source found.

sources.title: 1987 Buick GNX (profile by Tom Glatch, 1 January 2015)
Buick GNX: The Legend That Outshines Reality (Jim Campisano)

reviewNotes: Weight is a single article's curb weight used alongside Car and Driver's test times, not explicitly attributed; a Buick 1987 GNX specification or a major magazine spec panel should confirm it. The transmission speed count (4) is read from the 200-4R name, not stated on an opened page.
provisionalNote: Power (276 hp) rests on four articles agreeing (Sports Car Market, Street Muscle, Classic Industries, Conceptcarz); weight (3,545 lb) rests on a single article (Street Muscle) that uses it alongside Car and Driver's times. A Buick 1987 GNX press release or specification, or a major magazine spec panel, would replace them.
